chunks: And indeed I was with him (peace be upon him and his family),

when the leaders of Quraysh came to him and said to him, 'O Muhammad, you have made a great claim which none of your forefathers or anyone from your family made. We ask you one matter; if you answer us to it and show it to us, we will know that you are a prophet and a messenger, but if you do not do it, we will know that you are a sorcerer and a liar.'
ai.seo_question: What challenge did the leaders of Quraysh pose to Prophet Muhammad regarding his claim to prophethood?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha highlights the pragmatic skepticism of the Quraysh elite, who demanded empirical proof of prophethood to validate Muhammad’s claim, reflecting the broader Meccan context of testing divine messengers. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Quraysh’s demand for a 'sign' was not genuine seeking of truth but a pretext for dismissal, illustrating the theme of divine wisdom in choosing signs suited to the audience's capacity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: when a party of the Quraysh came to him and said to him, “O Muḥammad, you have made a big claim which none of your fore-fathers or those of your family have made. We ask you one thing; if you give us an answer to it and show it to us, we will believe that you are a prophet and a messenger, but if you cannot do it, we will know that you are a sorcerer and a liar.”
